title: Traffic Throttle Simulation & Dependency Chaos Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook defines a lightweight simulation and chaos experiment approach to validate launch readiness for traffic-throttle scenarios and downstream service dependencies. It’s meant to live as a mutable doc that product-ops, SRE, and release engineering iterate on during pre-launch and first-72h operations.

Scope and goals:
- Validate KPIs and guardrails under incremental traffic pressure (10% → 100%) for a feature launch.
- Exercise fallback and throttling policies end-to-end (API gateway → inference runtime → cache → downstream data services).
- Surface dependency failure modes that impact latency, error-rate, and cost.
- Produce actionable remediation playbooks and metric thresholds for go/no-go decisions.

Core assumptions (quick):
- Primary traffic path: Redwood API (hosted) → serving runtime pool (shared/dedicated) → embeddings cache → user DB for metadata.
- Canary cohort: 1% of traffic, progressive ramp to 10% then 50% during a dry-run window.
- Observability: per-route latency p50/p90/p99, token-cost per request, error-rate (4xx/5xx), queue lengths, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate.

KPIs to track in every simulation run (minimum fields):
- request_throughput_rps (string name for metric)
- p50_latency_ms
- p90_latency_ms
- p99_latency_ms
- downstream_error_rate_percent
- cache_hit_rate_percent
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd
- successful_responses_percent

(We record each KPI as a timeseries during steped traffic ramps.)

Simulation matrix (fast table for runs):
- run_id: run-01-canary (1% traffic)
  - intent: smoke + validate telemetry wiring
  - duration: 30 min
  - injected_faults: none
  - expected_actions: validate dashboards, collect baseline KPIs
- run_id: run-02-throttle-ramp (10% traffic)
  - intent: test autoscale & batching effects, observe token-cost impact
  - duration: 60 min
  - injected_faults: slow downstream DB (200ms added), KV cache miss surge (simulate 50% drop)
  - expected_actions: confirm autoscaler scales within target (target: CPU 70% / GPU mem 65%), check fallback model variant routing tripped correctly
- run_id: run-03-dependency-chaos (10% traffic)
  - intent: validate graceful degradation and fallback chain
  - duration: 45 min
  - injected_faults: 5xx from metadata DB for 10 minutes, partial network packet loss (2%)
  - expected_actions: serve degraded responses with cached metadata, verify errors are routed to fallback variant and throttled responses are returned with clear error codes for consumers
- run_id: run-04-surge-stress (50% traffic)
  - intent: stress throughput and observe cost + latency breakpoints
  - duration: 90 min
  - injected_faults: artificially double request payload length distribution (longer prompts), small quota starvation on dedicated pool (simulate 30% reduction in capacity)
  - expected_actions: activate overflow to hosted pool, ensure routing policy preserves SLAs for enterprise customers

Experiment orchestration checklist (pre-run):
- [ ] Confirm owner and oncall for run (ops lead, SRE, product-ops). Owner: Maya Rodriguez
- [ ] Create a dedicated dashboards snapshot and alert windows for the run period
- [ ] Post a run notice in #launch-control with run_id, start/end times, expected impact, roll-back link
- [ ] Backstop: feature flag toggles ready, circuit breaker policy tested in staging
- [ ] Backfill dataset: ensure test traffic uses synthetic but realistic prompt distributions and token lengths
- [ ] Confirm cost guardrail alert (auto-abort if cost-per-minute exceeds threshold)

During-run playbook (roles and responsibilities):
- Product-ops (Maya): overall run coordination, escalate to PMs if SLOs degrade beyond thresholds
- SRE lead (Ethan): monitor infra KPIs, trigger autoscale policy adjustments, execute capacity failover to backups
- Serving runtime eng (Lina): observe model runtime internals (KV cache hit ratios, KV eviction events), toggle quantization profiles if needed
- Solutions Eng / CS (Trevor): watch customer-visible errors, keep beta customers informed if they are in cohort

Run escalation ladder (fast):
- alert level 1: p90 latency > threshold (e.g., 2× baseline) for 5m → SRE investigate; scene-restore actions: reduce injection, switch to slower rollout
- alert level 2: p99 latency spike or 5xx tail errors > 1% for 2m → escalate to engineer on-call, consider draining canary traffic to 0%
- alert level 3: cost burn spike > guardrail (auto-abort) or sustained 50% capacity reduction without failover → abort run and initiate incident playbook

Dependency failure modes to validate (examples and expected mitigation):
- slow metadata DB: mitigation = serve stale metadata from cache + increase TTL for cache near-term; metric: successful_responses_percent must stay > 95%
- KV cache eviction storms: mitigation = temporary cache size bump for canary or pre-warm prefixes; metric: cache_hit_rate_percent should not fall below 60% for master routes
- model-serving OOMs on GPU: mitigation = fallback to quantized CPU variant or lower beam width; metric: p99_latency should remain within 3× baseline when fallback active

Post-run deliverables (automated + manual):
- automated: time-series export of KPIs, raw request traces for failed requests, alert timeline CSV
- manual: short run debrief (1 pager) with top 3 failure findings, recommended fixes and owners, decision recommendation (go / hold / partial rollout)

Decision rubric (quick):
- Green (proceed): p99 latency within baseline ×1.5, error-rate < 0.5%, cache_hit_rate > 70%, cost-per-1k-tokens within predicted band → proceed to gradual rollout
- Yellow (proceed with mitigations): p99 latency within ×2 and >95% successful responses; mitigation plan and re-run scheduled within 48h
- Red (hold): any single dependency causing >2% customer-visible errors or cost spiral above guardrail → hold and fix identified root causes

Templates (copy + paste snippets for run notes):
- Run notice (Slack): "Run notice: run_id=%s, window=%s-%s UTC, expected impact=canary 1%→10%, owners=Maya/Ethan/Lina, dashboards=LINK, rollback=feature-flag-xyz"
- Debrief header: "Run %s summary — top findings (TL;DR), KPIs (attached timeseries), recommended remediation and owners, go/hold recommendation."

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- [ ] Should we include an explicit budget throttle that auto-suspends runs for paid accounts? (ops/legal implication)
- [ ] Validate quick cold-start behaviors for rare long prompts (15k tokens simulated)
- [ ] Add a synthetic customer journey test: upstream web request → API → model → downstream DB update to validate full-stack correctness under failures

References and links (internal):
- Confluence: product-ops/traffic-throttle-sim (linked_artifacts above)
- Jira epic: JIRA-OPS-789
- Reference scripts: github:infra/traffic-sim#102

Appendix: quick glossary (for non-engineering readers)
- canary: a subset of traffic used for early validation
- KV cache: key-value cache used to store prefix/cache state for model context (improves throughput/cost)
- quantized variant: smaller/cheaper model serving binary used as fallback to reduce GPU memory/cost

Notes: This doc is intentionally procedural and will be converted to a one-click run template in the Console once we stabilize the orchestration scripts. For now, iterate here and update the linked scripts with run-ids and artifact hashes.
